explanation:
[EFFECT] Humidity has a non-monotonic (rises-then-falls) effect on predicted bike demand. Moderate humidity levels (roughly 20–75% relative humidity) are associated with a mild positive boost to demand, while very high humidity (above about 80%) sharply reduces predicted rentals — the contribution can drop as low as –0.7 in log space at near-saturation humidity. Very low humidity (below ~15%) also shows some negative contributions, though these hours are rare.

[IMPORTANCE] Humidity is the 6th most important feature out of 9, with a global importance score of 0.077. It has a moderate influence on demand — meaningful, but clearly less impactful than top features like hour or temperature.

[RECOMMENDATION] Pay close attention to forecasted humidity when planning staffing and bike availability: on days when humidity is expected to climb above 80%, significantly lower demand is likely, so over-stocking bikes or scheduling extra staff on those hours may not be necessary.
